title: From the Airport to Your Hotel
summary: AirTrain connects JFK airport terminals with Jamaica Station and Howard Beach. A subway journey can take you from these stations into Manhattan.

cover.alt: A traveller with a suitcase stands on a sunny platform near a train, a green subway entrance, and a warm hotel doorway in one continuous city scene.

blocks.title: Your journey into the city
paragraphs: AirTrain connects JFK airport terminals with Jamaica Station and Howard Beach. A subway journey can take you from these stations into Manhattan. Clear questions help you choose your connection, pay for travel, and explain what you need when you arrive.

items.prompt: How do you usually travel from an airport?
What do you say when you need travel help?
What would you like first after a long journey?

blocks.title: First, choose your connection
paragraphs: At JFK, AirTrain is the first part of this journey into the city. It connects the airport terminals with Jamaica Station and Howard Beach. Travel between airport terminals is free. Travel to Jamaica or Howard Beach has a separate fare. For a journey towards Midtown Manhattan, Jamaica Station and the E train are a clear choice. Another option is Howard Beach and the A train. These are different connections, so name the station when you ask for help. You can ask about Jamaica Station first, then ask which subway to take. This makes your question clear without a long explanation.

items.prompt: You want to travel towards Midtown Manhattan. What connection could you ask about, and why should you name the station?
items.answer: I could ask about AirTrain to Jamaica Station and then the E train. Naming Jamaica Station makes it clear which connection I want.
items.explanation: How would you ask a worker about that connection?

rows.term: Excuse me, I need help getting to Manhattan.
rows.meaning: A polite way to ask for help with your route into the city.
rows.example: Excuse me, I need help getting to Manhattan. Can you show me the way?

rows.term: Do I take AirTrain to Jamaica Station?
rows.meaning: Check that AirTrain is the right first step.
rows.example: Do I take AirTrain to Jamaica Station, or another train?

rows.term: Which subway do I take next?
rows.meaning: Ask which subway line comes after AirTrain.
rows.example: Which subway do I take next after Jamaica Station?

rows.term: So I take AirTrain first, then the E train. Thank you.
rows.meaning: Repeat the route to confirm you understand.
rows.example: So I take AirTrain first, then the E train. Thank you for your help.

blocks.title: Pay for each part
paragraphs: AirTrain and the subway are separate parts of your journey, with separate fares. The AirTrain fare to Jamaica Station or Howard Beach is $8.75. You pay that fare at those stations. You can use a contactless payment method or OMNY. The subway fare is $3, and you tap at the turnstile. Together, these two fares are $11.75 for this airport and subway journey. Keep the two payments clear when you ask for help. A useful question is whether a payment is for AirTrain or for the subway. You do not need a long speech to understand what you are paying for.

items.prompt: Someone explains the AirTrain payment. Why should you still ask about paying for the subway?
items.answer: AirTrain and the subway have separate fares. Paying for AirTrain does not pay for the subway, so I still need to tap at the subway turnstile.

rows.example: Is this payment for AirTrain, or for the subway?

rows.meaning: Ask if OMNY is accepted here.
rows.example: Can I pay with OMNY on this machine?

rows.term: Where do I tap for the subway?
rows.meaning: Ask where to tap your card to enter.
rows.example: Where do I tap for the subway at this station?

rows.term: Do I use the same card on the bus?
rows.meaning: Check if one card works for both subway and bus.
rows.example: Do I use the same card on the bus after the subway?

blocks.title: Keep the same card for a bus transfer
paragraphs: A local bus can be another part of a city journey after the subway. The subway and local bus fare is $3. A free transfer is available within two hours when you use the same card or device. On the subway, you tap at the turnstile. On a bus, you tap at the reader. If you paid with your phone on the subway, use that same device for the transfer. Changing to a different card does not follow the same-card rule. Before choosing a bus, explain where you want to go. This example does not give a bus route to a particular hotel.

items.prompt: You used your phone to pay for the subway and now want an eligible local bus transfer. What should you use on the bus, and why?
items.answer: I should tap the same phone at the bus reader. The free transfer rule requires the same card or device within two hours.

blocks.title: A drink, a snack, and a room
paragraphs: For this imagined arrival, the hotel has a café and a reception desk together. Coffee and a snack are available in this practice situation; this is not a claim about a real hotel. You arrive after travelling through Jamaica Station and taking the E train towards Manhattan. Now you can leave the travel questions behind and make two simple requests. First, ask for a coffee and a snack. Then explain that you have a reservation and want to check in. The worker can answer each request in order. Short, polite questions keep the exchange clear. You can finish by thanking the worker.

items.prompt: In the imagined hotel café, how can you ask for something to eat and also explain why you are at reception?
items.answer: I can say, ‘Could I have a coffee and a snack, please? I also have a reservation, and I’d like to check in.’

rows.term: Could I have a coffee and a snack, please?
rows.meaning: A polite way to order a drink and food.
rows.example: Could I have a coffee and a snack, please? To go.

rows.meaning: Tell the hotel you booked a room.
rows.example: I have a reservation under my name.

rows.term: I’d like to check in, please.
rows.meaning: Ask to start your hotel stay.
rows.example: I’d like to check in, please. Here is my passport.

rows.meaning: Show proof of your hotel booking.
rows.example: Here is my booking confirmation on my phone.

rows.meaning: End the conversation politely when you are done.
rows.example: Thank you. That’s everything for now.

blocks.title: At JFK: ask Leo for help
paragraphs: Airport help: you meet Leo, an airport worker, while choosing your connection to Manhattan. AirTrain links JFK with Jamaica Station, and the E train is a clear connection towards Midtown.
Your goal is to confirm the AirTrain and subway connection with Leo.

images.alt: A traveller with luggage asks an airport worker in a green vest near an elevated AirTrain platform inside a bright terminal.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me. I want to get to Midtown Manhattan. Can you help?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Yes. Take AirTrain to Jamaica Station, then take the E train towards Manhattan.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Does AirTrain go from the airport terminals to Jamaica Station?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: Yes, it connects the JFK terminals with Jamaica Station.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Is AirTrain free for that journey?

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: No. Travel between terminals is free, but the journey to Jamaica has a fare. You pay it at Jamaica Station.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: All right. AirTrain to Jamaica Station, then the E train. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: That’s the connection for this journey.

blocks.title: At Jamaica Station: ask Rosa about payment
paragraphs: Payment help: you meet Rosa, a transit worker, at Jamaica Station, where the AirTrain fare is paid separately from the subway fare. You plan to use OMNY for the subway and may make a local bus transfer, which requires the same card or device within two hours.
Your goal is to confirm both payments and choose one card or device for your subway and bus travel.

images.alt: A traveller taps a phone at a subway turnstile while speaking with a transit worker holding a folder.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hi. Is the payment here for AirTrain?

turns.speaker: Rosa
turns.text: Yes. The AirTrain fare at Jamaica Station is $8.75. The subway payment is separate.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Can I use OMNY for the subway?

turns.speaker: Rosa
turns.text: Yes. Tap at the subway turnstile. The subway fare is $3.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I may take a local bus after the subway. Can I use my phone for both?

turns.speaker: Rosa
turns.text: Yes. Use the same phone. A free transfer is available within two hours with the same card or device.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Where do I tap on the bus?

turns.speaker: Rosa
turns.text: At the bus reader.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Good. I’ll pay the AirTrain fare separately, then use the same phone for the subway and bus.

turns.speaker: Rosa
turns.text: Yes. That keeps your payments clear and follows the transfer rule.

blocks.title: At the imagined hotel: meet Maya
paragraphs: Hotel arrival: in this fictional situation, Maya works at a combined café and reception desk, with coffee and a snack available and your reservation ready. You arrived via AirTrain to Jamaica Station and the E train towards Manhattan, then made a local bus transfer within two hours using the same phone.
Your goal is to order a coffee and a snack, then complete your hotel check-in with Maya.

images.alt: A hotel café receptionist hands a room key to a traveller beside coffee and a snack on the counter.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Welcome. How was your journey?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Good, thanks. I took AirTrain to Jamaica Station, then the E train towards Manhattan.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: That is a clear connection towards Midtown. Did you also take a local bus?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes. I used the same phone within two hours for the free transfer.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Yes, that follows the transfer rule. What would you like now?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Could I have a coffee and a snack, please?

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Of course. Here are your coffee and snack.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. I also have a reservation. I’d like to check in.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Please show me your booking confirmation.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Here it is.

turns.speaker: Maya
turns.text: Thank you. Your check-in is complete. Here is your room key.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Great. Thank you for your help.

blocks.title: Tell a partner what you need

items.prompt: Travel conversation: you are explaining this journey to a partner. Say your AirTrain and subway connection, explain how you will pay for an eligible bus transfer, then make your café and hotel requests. Speak aloud, using your own words.
items.explanation: Include the connection through Jamaica Station, the same-card-or-device transfer rule, one polite food request, and one check-in request.

items.prompt: AirTrain connects JFK with Jamaica Station, where you can change to the E train towards Manhattan. An eligible subway-to-local-bus transfer uses the same card or device within two hours. Which request from this journey would you feel comfortable making, and which would you practise again?
items.explanation: Choose a route question, a payment question, a café request, or a check-in request. Explain your choice.

rows.meaning: A way to change from one service to another.
The money you pay for a journey.
rows.example: The subway has a separate fare.

rows.meaning: A gate you pass through to enter the subway.
A change from one form of transport to another.
rows.example: I want to make a bus transfer.

rows.meaning: An arrangement to have a room or service ready for you.
Tell a hotel that you have arrived and get access to your room.
